entities.name: Query protein (181 aa)
observations: Sequence length is 181 aa; estimated molecular weight is 20.28 kDa, theoretical pI 8.55, and charge at pH 7 is approximately +3.
Sequence contains multiple strongly hydrophobic segments, consistent with a compact multi-pass membrane protein.
Pfam PEMT domain PF04191.19 matches residues 75–172 with i-Evalue 9.1e-24.

Closest reviewed homologs include human PEMT Q9UBM1 at 39.5% identity over 91.7% query coverage, bovine PEMT Q7YRH6 at 37.5% identity over 92.8% coverage, and mouse PEMT Q61907 at 38.5% identity over 89.0% coverage.

Most likely function is phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase activity in phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis; this assignment is supported by homology and domain evidence, not direct experiment on the query sequence.
Likely localization is an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane, with possible mitochondrial-membrane association, based on reviewed homolog annotations.
Exact topology, oligomeric state, substrate specificity, and catalytic parameters are not directly established by this sequence analysis.

entities.name: Human PEMT Q9UBM1
observations: Reviewed human phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase; annotated as a multi-pass endoplasmic-reticulum membrane protein with mitochondrial-membrane localization also reported.
Catalyzes sequential SAM-dependent methylation of phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine through phosphatidylmonomethylethanolamine and phosphatidyldimethylethanolamine intermediates.

entities.name: Phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis
observations: PEMT-mediated sequential methylation contributes to phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis using S-adenosyl-L-methionine as methyl donor.
